testing_evidence.evidence: Fake-time scheduler cases cover first online, endpoint/config/control events, legacy capability absence, demand, global capacity, timeout, backoff, authority maintenance, stable reports and completion-based deadlines; real flow steps cover periodic issuance and legacy fallback.
Capability/result and directive roundtrip, legacy bases, existing optional tails and unsupported control payloads are exercised.
Registration refresh preserves the scheduler-owned profile beyond ten minutes and explicit invalidation removes publication.
Server authority and client gates cover TCP rejection, real TCP zero-directive flow, QUIC identity, online-before-probe, concurrent tunnels, endpoint bounds and fail-closed input.

Injected scheduler time proves the exact boundary, while the real QUIC flow forces that due state and proves exactly one directive, real UDP execution, correlated completion, and no immediate duplicate.
